about: This piece belongs to the formulary of the First Sunday of Advent, which opens the liturgical year in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: Stir up Your power, we beseech You, O Lord, and come, that we may deserve to be rescued from the threatening dangers of our sins under Your protection and to be saved by Your deliverance. Who live and reign with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

w010.function: The participle qualifies the dangers as already threatening. The whole phrase follows the preposition ab.

w016.function: With the first te it forms an ablative absolute: with You protecting. It gives the circumstance of the rescue.

w019.function: It forms a second ablative absolute with te, parallel to the protecting clause and governing the circumstance of salvation.

w032.note: The form is nominative and vocative at once. In this doxology it can be an apposition to the second-person subject or a direct address. This edition takes the nominative.
